question: Which of the following novels was written by Qurratulain Hyder in 1959 and is known for its deep insights on the Partition of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aag Ka Darya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aag Ka Darya** (River of Fire) was written by Qurratulain Hyder in 1959 and is considered one of the most important works in Urdu literature.
 
• The novel spans over two millennia, exploring the cultural, social, and political history of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is known for its profound examination of the effects of the **Partition of India (1947)** on individuals and society.
 
• The book delves deeply into themes of identity, displacement, and the continuity of civilization, connecting ancient and modern times.
 
• Qurratulain Hyder is often referred to as the **"Grande Dame of Urdu Literature"** for her contribution to the literary world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of India (1947):**

 
 
• The partition led to the division of British India into two independent dominions, India and Pakistan, causing massive displacement and communal violence.
 
• It remains one of the most significant and tragic events in South Asian history, affecting millions of lives.
 
 
 
• **Qurratulain Hyder:**
 
 
• Born in 1927, Hyder was an iconic Urdu novelist, short story writer, and translator, who received numerous accolades for her work, including the Jnanpith Award.
 
• Her literary contributions include novels like **"Mere Bhi Sanamkhane"** and **"Kar e Jahan Daraz Hai."**
 
 
 
• **Aag Ka Darya - Literary Style:**
 
 
• The novel utilizes a multi-layered narrative structure, intertwining historical and fictional elements.
 
• It incorporates characters from different time periods, blending personal stories with historical events.
 
 
 
• **Urdu Literature:**
 
 
• Urdu literature has a rich tradition of poetry and prose, with notable works in genres such as ghazals, novels, and short stories.
 
• Writers like Mirza Ghalib, Saadat Hasan Manto, and Ismat Chughtai have made significant contributions to Urdu literature.
